subject: HyperTransformer kickoff - few-shot personalization for small models
body:
Team,

Kicking off HyperTransformer. Core idea from our open-source release: a high-capacity transformer generates the weights of a small CNN directly from the support samples of a task, so the complexity of the task space lives in the transformer, not the tiny deployed model. That's a natural fit for on-device personalization: ship a small CNN, generate its weights per user/task in one shot, no on-device fine-tuning loop.

Scope this window: reproduce the supervised few-shot results on omniglot, miniImageNet and tieredImageNet; then evaluate the semi-supervised regime (unlabeled support samples) since real personalization data is mostly unlabeled; and produce a feasibility read on target-CNN sizes where the method actually wins.

Milestones: repro by mid-May, semi-supervised evaluation by late June, feasibility memo at the July 13 close. Deshawn owns staffing/compute; Carmen methodology; Vera experiments; Saoirse data tooling.

Lucia
